prompt:
Scene:
A square-format photograph of the same drained municipal indoor pool as the reference image, now at roughly 5:30 a.m. Weak sunrise light seeps through high clerestory windows, producing a low-contrast cyan-cream haze that fills the entire natatorium. The camera still uses a direct on-camera flash, which now acts as a fill against the ambient dawn rather than the only source. Mild 35mm film grain and a slightly greenish color cast persist.

Subject:
The identical six-lane empty basin seen from the exact same standing eye-level vantage. The same metal ladder is bolted at the near wall. The same cream deck tile surrounds the basin. The same ceramic wall tiles line the pool. Chlorine vapor hangs in the air as faint haze rising from the drain puddle. Dust motes are visible in the shaft of cold window light falling on the far deck.

Important details:
The tile pattern, lane painted stripes, ladder position, and camera viewpoint must exactly match the reference image — this is the same room rephotographed. Color temperature shifts from reference: add cool cyan ambient and reduce the flash dominance. Clerestory windows should read as high and narrow. Humidity must feel real. No swimmers, no staff, no photographer reflection. The uncanny note is that the space is full of morning light but nobody is using it.

Use case:
Series image 2 of 4. Preserves the reference basin under dawn ambient light with flash fill.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio, no swimmers, no staff, no added props, no warped tile perspective, no lens flare.
